summary: Intermittent p99 latency spike for repeated conversational turns; prefetch queue lagging on near-identical prompts
description:
Issue summary: Customers reporting repeated conversational turns (near-identical follow-ups) hitting p99 latency spikes and occasional 504s during generation. Symptoms began after a config change to the prefetch prioritizer (rolled 2026-03-12).

Impact: Multiple BrightDocs production routes observed 10-30x p99 increases on repeat turns; ~3% of requests in a time window returned 504 or streamed disconnect. Business impact: degraded user experience for active conversational sessions; BrightDocs CS flagged as Sev1.

Environment: prod (us-east region), Dedicated capacity cluster redwood-dedicated-us-east-5. Autoscaling healthy; CPU/GPU utilization normal. Issue confined to routes pinned to redwood/open-13B-v1 with session affinity enabled.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a multi-turn conversation with a short prompt (10-30 tokens).
2) Send near-identical follow-up prompts that only change a single token (e.g., punctuation or capitalization).
3) Observe increased latency on the second+ turn; high probability of hitting prefetch queue backpressure and falling back to cold KV read path.

Observed logs (redacted):
[2026-03-14T16:12:23Z] prefetcher.INFO id=xyz prefetch_enqueue delay_ms=12 queue_len=58 priority=low key=norm:turn:abcd123
[2026-03-14T16:12:23Z] kvcache.DEBUG id=xyz lookup_cache miss key=norm:turn:abcd123 shard=s3 ttl=0.0
[2026-03-14T16:12:25Z] serving-runtime.WARN id=xyz forward_to_cold_path reason=prefetch_timeout
[2026-03-14T16:12:28Z] api-gateway.ERROR id=xyz upstream=serving-runtime status=504 msg="generation timed out"

Initial hypothesis: The normalization/serialization step for KV keys is producing near-but-not-identical keys for follow-up turns (e.g., differing whitespace normalization and case). The prefetcher recently changed policy that deprioritizes prefetching for low-entropy variations which appears to interact poorly with queue scheduling under bursty conversational replay. This leads to increased cold-path reads, amplified lock contention on certain KV shards, and cascading queue backpressure culminating in request timeouts.

Why this is different from previous tickets: Existing tickets primarily described explicit TTL/eviction, shard rebalance, or hotkey storms. This incident correlates strongly with a prefetch prioritizer config change and with subtle key normalization drift (not a full TTL eviction). The cache misses are on keys that are semantically the same but serialized differently, causing wasted prefetch effort and lower cache hit ratio for repeat prompts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a short prompt and send it to BrightDocs route pinned to redwood/open-13B-v1. 2) Immediately send a follow-up that changes only case or trailing punctuation. 3) Observe p99 latency on second turn increase and check prefetcher metrics for enqueue delays.
investigation_notes: 03-14 17:00: Initial triage by Support (Avery) — correlated spikes to BrightDocs routes; escalated to SRE/Runtime.
03-14 18:10: Runtime team (Sofia) reproduced in staging with a scripted replay of 1k conversations; observed prefetch queue length growing and kvcache miss rate doubling for normalized keys.
03-14 19:45: Found config change merged 2026-03-12 (PR 1438) that modified prefetch prioritizer thresholds and lowered prefetch priority for low-entropy keys.
03-14 21:20: Discovered normalization codepath produced two canonical forms for whitespace-trimmed vs. unicode-normalized tokens; integration tests missed this edge-case.
03-15 08:05: Instrumented additional telemetry on KV key canonicalization and added a histogram for key variations per session.
03-15 10:00: Observed that fixing the prefetch priority to previous thresholds in a canary reduced p99 by ~60% for the test workload.
comments: Avery Chen (Support) 2026-03-14: Customer first reported ~16:10 UTC, attaching sample request IDs and logs. Marked as P1 and escalated.
Sofia Patel (Runtime) 2026-03-14: Reproduced locally. Prefetch queue grows when many near-identical keys are enqueued quickly; suspect prefetch deprioritization + key divergence.
Evan Morales (SRE) 2026-03-14: Temporarily increased prefetch worker concurrency on redwood-dedicated-us-east-5 at 20:30 UTC which reduced error rate for BrightDocs by ~50%.
Maya Singh (Customer Success) 2026-03-14: Informed BrightDocs of investigation and temporary mitigation; requested to postpone heavy campaigns until fix.
Sofia Patel (Runtime) 2026-03-15: Preparing a small rollback patch for prefetch priority and a follow-up normalization fix. Will open PR for normalization canonicalizer tests.
root_cause: Interaction of a prefetch prioritizer change (lowering priority for low-entropy keys) with a subtle key canonicalization inconsistency. Near-identical follow-up prompts produced different serialized KV keys which prevented efficient cache hits and increased cold-path reads and shard lock contention.
temporary_workaround: Scaled prefetch worker concurrency and manually adjusted prefetch prioritizer thresholds back to previous values for the affected cluster; recommended customers avoid short-burst identical-replay campaigns until fix applied.
resolution: In progress: rollout plan includes (1) revert prioritizer threshold change as an immediate rollback (canary first), (2) deploy normalization patch with additional unit/integration tests to ensure single canonical form for near-identical conversational turns, and (3) add telemetry and alert on key-variation ratio per session. Targeting full fix deployment 2026-03-17.
postmortem_followups: Add unit tests for canonicalization edge-cases and enforce in CI
Create alerting rule: kvcache.key_variants_per_session > 3 for 5m => pager
Run a runbook update to include prefetched-queue backpressure mitigation steps
Coordinate with Customer Success to notify impacted enterprise customers and provide remediation timeline
